ev_02676ed71188.description: Two-Way Mirror books celebrates the release of its latest books: Danny Rosen 's A Love Poem Called War and J Grabowski 's POMPEI: or The Notes Are In The World , with music by J Lee's Starry Skemes . Publisher Marina Lazzara hosts. Each morning Danny Rosen pees on the bank of the largest unnamed tributary to the East Branch of Big Salt Wash which flows into the Colorado River several miles below Fruita, Colorado. Early on he learned to swing a hammer and that changed everything. He has been a poet, publisher, teacher, geologist, astronomer, and carpenter. In the middle of his journey he found himself running an astronomical observatory in the heart of the Namib Desert under the southern sky where he cultivated an optimistic outlook based on his familiarity with big space and deep time. He is the author of Suspended Erosion (2024), The Tuscan Journals & Other Poems (2022), Primate Poems (2016), Ghosts of Giant Kudu (2013), and That Curve (2006). He founded Lithic Press in 2007 and has run Lithic Bookstore since its opening in 2015. An inveterate rock hanger, he has collaborated with beavers on a variety of landscape installations. ev_04a1629ae14e.description: Jack Crimmins is the Sonoma County-based author of seven poetry collections, including his latest trilogy, "The Light in California" (Taurean Horn Press). In her introduction to his first book, "Kit Fox Blues," Diane di Prima wrote, "Jack Crimmins weaves together the music of the city streets and the urgent, fragile sounds of wilderness." Melissa Eleftherion (she/they) is a writer, a librarian, and a visual artist. Born & raised in Brooklyn, she is the author of four poetry collections: field guide to autobiography (The Operating System, 2018), gutter rainbows (Querencia Press, 2024), Suture (Cooper Dillon, 2026) & Malocchia (White Stag, 2026) as well as twelve chapbooks including abject sutures (above/ground press, 2024). Her work has been widely published, & recently appeared/is forthcoming in the Academy of American Poets' Poem-a-Day series, DIAGRAM, & Sixth Finch. Melissa served as Poet Laureate for the City of Ukiah (2021-2024), and lives in Northern California where she manages the Ukiah Branch Library and curates the LOBA Reading Series. ev_065c0216bfa4.description: The Cookers bring expressive language to the bandstand and to their six critically acclaimed recordings: Warriors, Cast the First Stone, Believe, Time and Time Again , The Call of the Wild and Peaceful Heart and Look Out! . This exciting all-star septet summons up an intense mid-60s spirit with a potent collection of post-bop originals marked by the requisite instincts and pyrotechnic playing expected of these heavy hitters. Eddie Henderson , Cecil McBee , George Cables , and Billy Hart all came up in the heady era of the mid-60s as members of some of the most important bands of the era. Hart and Henderson were members of Herbie Hancock's groundbreaking Mwandishi group; Cecil McBee anchored Charles Lloyd's great '60s quartet alongside Keith Jarrett and Jack DeJohnette; while Cables held down the piano chair in numerous bands including groups led by Sonny Rollins, Joe Henderson, Freddie Hubbard, Dexter Gordon and Art Pepper. David Weiss , Donald Harrison , and Azar Lawrence , from a more recent generation, are experts in this forthright lingo, having gained experience performing with Art Blakey, Bobby Hutcherson, Freddie Hubbard, Charles Tolliver, Roy Haynes and Herbie Hancock. ev_084d16ec6dea.description: The Garage Jam is an open, friendly bluegrass circle that meets the first and third Monday of every month, from 6 to 8 pm. All kinds of pickers show up, from rank beginners to grizzled veterans, plus folks who just come to listen and socialize. The repertoire is straight-up traditional bluegrass, although the occasional old-time or folk-inflected choice will pop up. The format is the old-fashioned song circle, with each participant getting a turn to call a song and set its key, pace, and feel. An experienced jam leader and bass player are always present to help keep things on track. Everyone is welcome — come on down!

Sung's "Oracles Quartet" distills this music for small group, while including the music of a living oracle (or two) as well. Like a hip-hop link up from the 90s, the pair's collective ear, musical talents, and friendship pushes the limits of the R&B organ trio sound into a youthful, tasty style of 'blue collar jazz.' Fonville x Fribush features a rotating cast of guitarists in the studio, including Charlie Hunter, Alan Good Parker and Morgan Burrs. Songs like "I Couldn't Love You More" and "Blue Chips" immerse audiences in Atlantic Coast soundscapes of their hometown roots in North Carolina and Virginia. In 2026, they released their debut Fonville x Fribush EP, R&B Organ Trio , featuring Charlie Hunter. ev_0f57b87eb7a8.description: Held on 2nd Saturdays,12-3pm, at 1005 Railroad Ave, in Santa Clara, CA. The Santa Clara Historic Train Depot, Bluegrass, Country, Old Time, & Folk jam is free and open to intermediate and experienced stringed instrument players. The jam started in 2012, and is now on its 11th year. The The South Bay Historic Railroad Society kindly lends chairs and space for the jam. The jam takes place on the patio on sunny days in front of the historic depot and train museum. When the weather is inclement, the jam moves into the train museum. Parking is free in front of the depot museum, $5.50 if you park in the caltran parking lot.

All kinds of pickers show up, from rank beginners to grizzled veterans, plus folks who just come to listen and socialize. The repertoire is straight-up traditional bluegrass, although the occasional old-time or folk-inflected choice will pop up. The format is the old-fashioned song circle, with each participant getting a turn to call a song and set its key, pace, and feel. ev_1f2d8e91b4b9.description: Take a comfy seat and celebrate the grand finale of SF Stairway Month hearing authors Mary Burk (Stairway Walks in San Francisco) and Alexandra Kenin (Urban Trails series, San Francisco, East Bay, Peninsula and South Bay). And sharpen your wits: We will have special SF stairway trivia game designed by moderator Liz Novoa (aka Instagram's staircase queen). Mary and Alex will delight you with stories of SF's known and hidden stairways, tell you about the best views, and share the whereabouts of secret gardens and more. Mary enjoyed a longstanding partnership with Adah Bakalinsky, co-authoring these now renowned stairway books until Adah's passing at over 100 years old. Alex is the embodiment of energy. In addition to highlights from her book(s), she will share her detailed map of everything that you have wanted to know about SF's roughly1000 stairways. This event is organized by Glen Park Beautiful (www.gpbeautiful.org). It is the 3rd annual SF Stairway Month, which was inspired by the creation of Glen Park's Burnside Tiled Steps. The event is also featured in this inaugural year of Walktober, a month-long celebration of guided walks in San Francisco hosted by the Crosstown Trail .

ev_206052f131ad.description: Over the course of a multifaceted career spanning four decades, GRAMMY- and TONY-winning jazz giant Dee Dee Bridgewater has ascended to the upper echelon of vocalists, putting her unique spin on standards, as well as taking intrepid leaps of faith in re-envisioning jazz classics. Bridgewater's career has always bridged musical genres. She earned her first professional experience as a member of the legendary Thad Jones/Mel Louis Big Band, and throughout the '70s she performed with such jazz notables as Max Roach, Sonny Rollins, Dexter Gordon, and Dizzy Gillespie. After a foray into the pop world during the 1980s, she relocated to Paris and began to turn her attention back to jazz. Signing with Universal Music Group as a producer (Bridgewater produces all of her albums), Bridgewater released a series of critically acclaimed titles beginning with Keeping Tradition in 1993. All but one – including her wildly successful double GRAMMY Award-winning tribute to Ella Fitzgerald, Dear Ella – have received GRAMMY nominations. ev_267726303eda.description: Kurt Rosenwinkel is a highly acclaimed and influential jazz guitarist, composer, and bandleader. Hailed as one of the most important jazz musicians of his generation, Rosenwinkel has spent decades pushing the boundaries of the jazz genre and developing a signature sound that has captivated audiences worldwide. With a career spanning over thirty years, Rosenwinkel has released a series of groundbreaking albums, collaborated with jazz legends, and continues to inspire the next generation of jazz musicians. Gerald Clayton suggests a new ideal and a promising way forward in modern jazz. A pianist, composer, and seven-time GRAMMY nominee, he stands out for his ability to balance heritage and innovation; bridging the tradition he grew up in and a fearless sense of exploration. As a bandleader, he's created music that ranges from the intimate reflections of Bells on Sand to the electrifying immediacy of Happening: Live at the Village Vanguard . Together, Kurt Rosenwinkel and Gerald Clayton present a very special evening guitar-piano duets. Kurt Rosenwinkel Website Gerald Clayton Website Sponsored by Rosalind & Howard Fisher (Ticket Includes 5% City of Santa Cruz Admission Tax) .embed-cont
ev_267726303eda.title: Kurt Rosenwinkel & Gerald Clayton

ev_2894cc6b65c6.description: Gabrielle Cavassa is a singer and composer from Escondido, California. She was ushered into the spotlight through her collaboration with renowned saxophonist Joshua Redman on his 2023 record where are we . In a five-star album review by DownBeat , Cavassa is hailed as "a young singer with a deep, rich, and fragile voice...a star in the making." Cavassa began "obsessively listening" to records from a young age. Largely self-taught, she developed a unique approach to singing that would later characterize her artistry. Cavassa received a Bachelor of Arts in Music from San Francisco State University, but credits the Bay Area music scene for her "real education." In 2020, Cavassa independently released an eponymous debut record produced by collaborator Jamison Ross. In 2021, she was crowned a winner of the prestigious International Sarah Vaughan Jazz Vocal Competition. Later that year she was discovered by Redman's manager at an event in New Orleans, leading to their collaboration on the 2023 record. After its release, Cavassa toured extensively across the world with the Joshua Redman Group. Blue Note signed Cavassa in 2024, quoting label president Don Was: "listening to Gabrielle sing

ev_296af491eefb.description: On this rare concert date, Vijay Iyer and Wadada Leo Smith revisit the music from their collaborative albums – 2016's A Cosmic Rhythm With Each Stroke, and 2025's Defiant Life – for this evening of duets. Of Defiant Life , Pitchfork writes that "The second collaborative album by the jazz composers and instrumentalists is a searching meditation on resistance and revolutionary potential." Described by The New York Times as a "social conscience, multimedia collaborator, system builder, rhapsodist, historical thinker and multicultural gateway," Vijay Iyer has carved out a unique path as an influential, prolific, shape-shifting presence in twenty-first century music. A composer and pianist active and revered across multiple musical communities, Iyer has created a consistently innovative, emotionally resonant body of work over the last three decades, earning him a place as one of the leading music-makers of his generation. Iyer's musical language is indebted to the great composer-pianists from Duke Ellington to Alice Coltrane, the rhythmic traditions of South Asia and West Africa, and the African American creative music movement of the sixties and seventies. ev_2d96d87856a4.description: Lucía is a 24-year-old vocalist from Veracruz, México whose singular artistic vision bridges the gaps between jazz, latin, and pop music. Lucía Gutierrez Rebolloso started her musical career at the age of two, singing and dancing in her parents' son jarocho band, Son de Madera. She began studying voice at the age of thirteen at Universidad Veracruzana, and in 2022 received a Bachelor's degree in Jazz Studies from this same university. In 2022, she became the first artist from Mexico to enter the Sarah Vaughan International Jazz Vocal Competition, which she won. Lucía has already collaborated with several world-renowned artists and musicians, including Natalia Lafourcade, Aloe Blacc, La Santa Cecilia, Quetzal, Son de Madera, Alex Mercado, and the National Jazz Orchestra of Mexico. Most recently, Lucía has just released her first full album. Produced by GRAMMY-winner Matt Pierson, it presents Lucía's interpretations of jazz standards (such as "What a Difference a Day Makes" and "You Must Believe in Spring") classic Spanish songs (including "Silencio" and "La Llorona") and current pop songs. ev_2f4e443442f0.description: James Gordon Williams is an acclaimed composer and pianist whose performances span leading jazz clubs, concert halls, theaters, and international festivals throughout the United States and Europe. He has performed with distinguished artists including Terri Lyne Carrington and Anthony Davis, and has appeared at iconic venues including Birdland and the Village Vanguard. As a theatre composer, he has written music for Syracuse Stage's production of Kyle Bass's salt/city/blues . His transdisciplinary collaborations include projects with Crystal Z. Campbell, Maria Gaspar, Mariachi Eterno, Moor Mother, Fred Moten, Cauleen Smith, and Suné Woods. Williams is also the author of Crossing Bar Lines: The Politics and Practices of Black Musical Space (2021), and is an Associate Professor of Music at the University of California, Santa Cruz, and holds a Ph.D. from the University of California, San Diego. Williams' forthcoming album, Falling to Rise Again , will be released this year. The album is Williams' musical meditation on resilience—the enduring capacity to move forward through life's inevitable uncertainties. ev_2f7285cb655b.description: DINNER SHOW with MIKO MARKS: Hell or High Water Tour/ Rancho Debut! Rolling Stone has called Miko Marks ' voice a "marvelous instrument that imbues each song with a kind of hard-won authority." Across a career defined by resilience, reinvention, and a refusal to let the music industry dictate where she belongs, Marks has built a singular musical identity rooted in country, gospel, blues, and soul. Born and raised in Flint, Michigan, she is a granddaughter of the Great Migration whose Southern family roots and musical upbringing continue to inform her work. "Blues is a part of who I am," Marks says. "It's woven into my upbringing, my experiences, and my musical journey."

ev_30a270279b9a.description: Award-winning violinist Eva Slongo and guitarist Jimmy Grant present an intimate and swinging set rooted in the gypsy jazz tradition of Django Reinhardt and Stéphane Grappelli. For this concert they're joined by special guest Simon Planting on bass. Their music draws equally from European jazz, Eastern European folk influences, and classic vocal jazz, resulting in a sound that feels both timeless and accessible to modern audiences. A defining element of their collaboration is the integration of vocals. In addition to her virtuosic violin playing, Eva incorporates scat singing and vocal improvisation in a subtle, musical style reminiscent of George Benson. At times she sings while playing, adding a distinctive and engaging layer that resonates strongly with jazz audiences. Their repertoire includes French chanson, swing standards, and original arrangements that evoke travel, nostalgia, and joy. Expect a warm, dynamic performance that emphasizes groove, melody, and connection. info/tickets/questions: contact presenter .embed-container { position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; max-width: 100%; } .embed-container iframe, .embed-container object, .embed-

ev_30c809f01b96.description: Nicole McCabe is a genre-defying saxophonist and composer bringing the expressive power of modern jazz into dialogue with the sonic worlds of electronic, indie, and experimental music. Through her work as a bandleader, collaborator, and composer, Nicole McCabe continues to expand the possibilities of the saxophone in contemporary music. With a voice that honors tradition while pushing boldly into new sonic territory, she represents a new generation of artists redefining what modern jazz can be. As a performer, McCabe brings a distinctive sound to the alto saxophone, one that draws equally from the lineage of post-bop masters and the forward-looking spirit of today's creative music scenes. Her playing is marked by clarity, intensity, and emotional depth, capable of moving fluidly from delicate melodic phrasing to fiery, rhythmically charged improvisation. Whether performing in intimate acoustic settings or within electronically enhanced ensembles, McCabe's presence is both commanding and deeply communicative. McCabe's collaborative range is unusually broad. Rooted in jazz but unconfined by it, she regularly works across musical worlds – performing with jazz innovators, pop artists,
ev_30c809f01b96.title: Nicole McCabe Quartet

ev_30d7cb5b66a0.description: An evening of new music for stringed traditional East Asian instruments. Featuring Katherine Whatley (koto and voice), Southeast of Rain (pipa, voice, electronics), and Stella Da Yun Song (haegeum). About the performers and pieces: Katherine Whatley Katherine Whatley is a koto musician, composer, and PhD Candidate in East Asian Languages and Cultures at Stanford University. She plays both traditional and experimental koto, both improvised and composed. Her compositions have been performed by the Stanford New Ensemble and the Earplay Ensemble. She has performed in a variety of contexts including at the Good Shepherd Center (Seattle), Columbia University (New York), on tour across Japan and in Berlin. Her dissertation analyzes music and soundscape in medieval Japanese literature. Her research has previously been published in The February Journal, positions, Japanese Journal of Religious Studies, and Migrating Minds. As a journalist, she has worked with the BBC, Dwell, Conde Nast, New York Times, the Japan Times, and others. 今、箏ひびき(Ima Koto Hibiki)—Now, Here Koto Sings This piece for 13-string koto and voice is based on Ryōjin Hisho, a 12th-century collection of imayō (popular songs).

ev_313eeb115be8.description: The Garage Jam is an open, friendly bluegrass circle that meets the first and third Monday of every month, from 6 to 8 pm. All kinds of pickers show up, from rank beginners to grizzled veterans, plus folks who just come to listen and socialize. The repertoire is straight-up traditional bluegrass, although the occasional old-time or folk-inflected choice will pop up. The format is the old-fashioned song circle, with each participant getting a turn to call a song and set its key, pace, and feel. An experienced jam leader and bass player are always present to help keep things on track. Everyone is welcome — come on down!

ev_3ee4a4c76c3b.description: Born and raised in Madrid, Spain, pianist and composer Marta Sánchez is actively working in the contemporary creative music scene in New York City and around the globe. Charting a significant path through her innovative and original music, she has reached an international audience and gained significant global recognition. Sánchez, the 2025 DownBeat Critics Poll 'Rising Star' in piano, leads a quintet on this concert date featuring Devon Gates on vocals, Alex LoRe on alto saxophone, Roman Filiu on tenor saxophone, Rashaan Carter on bass, and Allan Mednard on drums. The group has released five albums, two of them selected by The New York Times among the ten best records of their respective release years. Sánchez is currently presenting the music of her latest album, Shamanism , in which she expands the quintet with vocals, combining her music with lyrics that address often-unspoken experiences, including depression, infertility, and ageism, among others. ev_3fd3b077d537.description: "Raw, underground, and chaotic...one of modern jazz music's most audacious futurists." – Pitchfork Revered by living icons and underground tastemakers, Kassa Overall began his career behind the drum kit. At the Oberlin Conservatory of Music, Overall spent his days studying jazz drums and music theory, and his evenings making beats in his dorm room, often staying home from parties to pull all-nighters in front of his MPC, studio monitors, and an open Pro Tools session. At Oberlin, he met musicians who remain his closest musical collaborators to this day. Overall's groundbreaking solo projects have established him as a driving force on the international stage, fielding support from visionaries including Thom Yorke, Iggy Pop, Virgil Abloh, and more. His first studio album, GO GET ICE CREAM AND LISTEN TO JAZZ (2019) bore witness to the emergence of a sound that layered the virtuosic drumming, polyrhythmic rapping, and meticulous production techniques he had honed separately. On 2020's I THINK I'M GOOD , his voice continued to crystallize, critiquing the injustices of the carceral system, the pharmaceutical industry, and anti-black racism. With ANIMALS , released in 2023 on Warp Records

ev_4286a05dfc3e.description: Kim Shuck conducts the twice-monthly Virtual Poets series, with featured readers followed by an open mic on the 2nd Monday of each month and an all-open mic session on the 4th Monday of each month. Kim embraces the fool and jester qualities of being a modern poet and artist. She is a devotee of San Francisco, whose hills she wanders nearly always on foot. Her maternal grandparents met at the Polish Hall on Shotwell and she spent many hours with her mother and grandmother wandering the Mission St. Miracle Mile, taking books out of the Mission Branch library and watching aquarium fish on the ground floor of what used to be Hale's. She firmly believes in carrying a bubble wand, keys, pen and notebook and cats cradle string at all times. Kim, whose poetry draws on her multiethnic background which includes Polish and Cherokee heritage, and her experiences as a lifelong resident of San Francisco, served as San Francisco's seventh Poet Laureate, from 2017-2021. ev_43cb5127d7c0.description: Ella Dair is a NYC-based jazz vocalist. Originally from San Francisco, she started singing at a young age, performing with many Bay Area legends in her aunt's swing band "Lavay Smith & Her Red Hot Skillet Lickers." Ella continued her education in music and performance with SFArtsEd, falling in love with the songs of Harold Arlen and Kander & Ebb, among other classics of the Great American Songbook. As a teenager she was a vocal soloist with the youth choir at Glide Memorial, the renowned non-denominational church presided over by civil rights leader Cecil Williams. Ella earned her bachelor's degree from Bard College, studying anthropology and Latin American studies with a particular interest in ethnomusicology. Her studies broadened her musical tastes and sent her to Mexico City, where she lived post-grad. Ella then moved to New York City, joining the staff at Dizzy's Club at Jazz At Lincoln Center, where she has been exposed to many of the greatest jazz musicians in the world. ev_46a325042b09.description: THE STELLA HEATH CHRISTMAS SHOW – Billie Holiday/ Ella Fitzgerald Tribute! This special performance will be a heartfelt homage to ELLA FITZGERALD the First Lady of Song, blending her timeless music with fascinating historical stories and meticulous research. Stella and her quintet will also present the music of BILLIE HOLIDAY. Shrouded in mystery as she was draped in fur, Billie was multi-faceted; she possessed a sensitivity and ability to make the songs she sang as personal as if she was singing them softly in your very own ear. Featuring some of the Bay Area's finest Jazz musicians, Stella's quintet brings back the electric and intimate feeling of seeing Lady Day live in a 1930's Jazz Club.

ev_46ae60194a66.description: A multimedia presentation of Japanese art and live jazz by the Fumi Tomita Quartet. Fumi Tomita, bass Carl Clements, woodwinds Jason Ennis, guitars Gary Fieldman, drums Fumi Tomita is a jazz bassist, composer, educator, and author. His newest recording, Yokai! Songs of the Japanese Supernatural will be released in October 2026 on Origin records and was inspired by 19th-century woodblock prints of Yokai and other Japanese supernatural creatures derived from folklore. The album will be supported by a Northeast tour during October and November. His 2019 recording, The Elephant Vanishes: Jazz Interpretations of the Short Stories of Haruki Murakami, was released to critical acclaim by Origin Arts records and was listed in the top ten records of 2019 by Jazziz. His 2020 release Celebrating Bird: The Music of Charlie Parker was similarly received. Tomita was active on the New York city jazz scene for over fifteen years and has performed at venues all over the U.S. and Canada including recent appearances at the International Society of Bassists Conference in Ann Harbor, Michigan in June 2023 and the Jazz Education Network conference in New Orleans and a short tour of Georgia, both in Janua

ev_490541862f7a.description: Paul Hanson, reeds; Joel Harrison, guitar; Michael Manring, bass; Scott Amendola, drums Former Berkeley resident, guitarist Joel Harrison, returns to the Bay Area to journey into Miles Davis' iconic 1970 record, "In a Silent Way." The band consists of old allies, some of the Bay Area's finest and most creative musicians—they will also perform some of Harrison's original music. Harrison recently released a live record from the Big Ears Festival of this music. The band's approach will be to "make it new." Guitarist, composer, arranger, lyricist, writer, educator and vocalist Joel Harrison has "created a new blueprint for jazz" (New Orleans Times-Picayune). He has released 27 records, a body of work that connects multiple American traditions. While rooted in jazz, his music moves fluidly through classical, rock, country, and American roots music. The New York Times has described his work as "protean... brilliant." Harrison is the founder and director of the Alternative Guitar Summit, an annual festival devoted to innovative and unconventional guitar music. The Summit has featured artists such as Fred Frith, Nels Cline, Bill Frisell, Julian Lage, Michael Gregory Jackson, Mary Halvorson

ev_49ee9b2a2593.description: The Garage Jam is an open, friendly bluegrass circle that meets the first and third Monday of every month, from 6 to 8 pm. All kinds of pickers show up, from rank beginners to grizzled veterans, plus folks who just come to listen and socialize. The repertoire is straight-up traditional bluegrass, although the occasional old-time or folk-inflected choice will pop up. The format is the old-fashioned song circle, with each participant getting a turn to call a song and set its key, pace, and feel. An experienced jam leader and bass player are always present to help keep things on track. Everyone is welcome — come on down!

ev_4b3b984c2a8e.description: Honored by The National Endowment for the Arts as a 2010 Jazz Master, Kenny Barron has an unmatched ability to mesmerize audiences with his elegant playing, sensitive melodies and infectious rhythms. The Los Angeles Times named him "one of the top jazz pianists in the world" and Jazz Weekly calls him "The most lyrical piano player of our time." The Philadelphia native started playing professionally as a teenager with Mel Melvin's orchestra and Philly Joe Jones. He moved to New York City at nineteen and freelanced with Roy Haynes, Lee Morgan and James Moody, after the tenor saxophonist heard him play at the Five Spot. Upon Moody's recommendation Dizzy Gillespie hired Barron in 1962 without even hearing him play a note. It was in Dizzy's band where Barron developed an appreciation for Latin and Caribbean rhythms. After five years with Dizzy, Barron played with Freddie Hubbard, Stanley Turrentine, Milt Jackson, and Buddy Rich. By 1973, Barron joined the faculty at Rutgers University as professor of music. ev_55f25ffc10f7.description: Delbert Anderson , a Diné jazz trumpet artist, composer, and educator, stands at the forefront of a vibrant Native American jazz scene. His work, deeply rooted in his Diné heritage, seamlessly integrates Navajo "spinning songs" of love, healing, and courtship with jazz and funk. With his Delbert Anderson Quartet, Anderson revives the improvised sounds of the Diné circle, blending them with jazz, funk, and hip-hop. His compositions are inspired by Navajo Nation landscapes, historical events, and the desire to preserve and educate about Diné history. This evening will be celebrating Anderson's recent album Live at Kuumbwa Jazz , recorded on our stage. Anderson's other notable projects include "The Long Walk: 1,674 Days," a poignant composition reflecting on a critical period in Navajo history. His commitment to community and education is evident through his "Build A Band" educational program, which teaches jazz improvisation to young students through a Diné and family curriculum, wellness programs, and community outreach initiatives aimed at evoking change for the well-being of all humans. ev_563acd5e6404.description: Hailed as "the future of guitar," Alex Misko is a modern fingerstyle guitar prodigy who mesmerizes audiences worldwide. From viral videos with over 80 million views to performing at Carnegie Hall and collaborating with Hans Zimmer, his music captivates fans online and at live shows around the globe. Still in his 20s, Misko has gained international recognition with seven albums, a YouTube channel exceeding a million subscribers, and performances spanning from America to Japan. He's known for his innovative Frankenstein Guitar, a one-of-a-kind acoustic instrument featuring a triple detuning system, built-in percussion, and 14 pickups. With a style that blends technical innovation with accessible musicality, Misko's compositions transcend cultural barriers and speak a universal language wherever they are heard. A must-see for fans of instrumental brilliance, next-level guitar playing, and world-class musical storytelling. They have performed at many of the great performing arts centers, festivals, and venues around the world. Salsa Navidad is a show dedicated to classic Latinx music as well as select American Christmas classics done in a salsa style. Part of the show features the Puerto Rican Christmas style known as "Aguinaldo," which reflects the spirit and cultural essence of the Caribbean. This concert program also features the ensemble's non-holiday, original music for which they have become so well known for. ev_57cf0eab1e02.description: Meshell Ndegeocello's first two Blue Note albums – The Omnichord Real Book (2023) and No More Water: The Gospel Of James Baldwin (2024) – have persuasively reasserted her status as an unparalleled force in modern music, earning her the first two GRAMMY Awards to honor her own albums in her three-decade long recording career; exploding any remaining notions of genre boundaries, and coalescing a tight-knit creative circle that operates collectively in the spirit of their motto: Meshell Ndegeocello is a band. With her latest album, Synonym , Ndegeocello reaches even higher to deliver one of the most ambitious projects in her impressive discography by expanding her cast of collaborators to include an astounding rollcall of featured guests. At its core, the album captures her ingenuity in reimagining and reconceptualizing songs written and performed by other musicians. Exploring expressions of desire, care, heartbreak, friendship, disappointment, and love in all forms, this thoughtfully curated collection of covers ranges from '60s folk and '70s soul, country, and pop to '80s R&B and electro-boogie, early '90s alternative rock, and early aughts hip-hop. ev_584ddd7aa200.description: Pianist and two-time GRAMMY nominee Christian Sands is an emerging jazz force. His abundant piano technique perfectly matches his ambition, accomplishing a much deeper musical goal: a fresh look at the entire spectrum of jazz. A protégé of Dr. Billy Taylor, Sands released his debut album at the age of twelve. He came to wider prominence through his work as a member of two bands led by iconic bassist Christian McBride: the Christian McBride Trio and Inside Straight. Sands has shared the stage with such jazz luminaries as Wynton Marsalis, Dianne Reeves, and Sheila E, among many others. Sands is celebrating the release of Christmas Stories , his first album of holiday both songs old and new. While Sands views Christmas as a time of nostalgia, reflection and reunion, he also recognizes it as a time for renewal and looking ahead. Christmas Stories is Sands' fifth release for Mack Avenue, following Reach (2017), Facing Dragons (2018), the GRAMMY-nominated Be Water (2020), and Embracing Dawn (2023). ev_5ad8674474af.description: Kim Shuck conducts the twice-monthly Virtual Poets series, with featured readers followed by an open mic on the 2nd Monday of each month and an all-open mic session on the 4th Monday of each month. Kim embraces the fool and jester qualities of being a modern poet and artist. She is a devotee of San Francisco, whose hills she wanders nearly always on foot. Her maternal grandparents met at the Polish Hall on Shotwell and she spent many hours with her mother and grandmother wandering the Mission St. Miracle Mile, taking books out of the Mission Branch library and watching aquarium fish on the ground floor of what used to be Hale's. She firmly believes in carrying a bubble wand, keys, pen and notebook and cats cradle string at all times. Kim, whose poetry draws on her multiethnic background which includes Polish and Cherokee heritage, and her experiences as a lifelong resident of San Francisco, served as San Francisco's seventh Poet Laureate, from 2017-2021. In 2019, she was awarded an inaugural National Laureate Fellowship from the Academy of American Poets, and a PEN Oakland Censorship Award. ev_5b4be1733d61.description: Different Strokes for Different Folks marks a full-circle moment for Ella Feingold , who first saw Charlie Hunter performing with Leon Parker at the Regatta Bar in the late '90s. She never imagined that decades later she'd be playing and recording alongside him as both a peer and a friend. Today, Hunter describes her as "one of the baddest, greasiest guitar players on the planet." This exploratory duo project is a deep dive into the art of musical conversation. Built on a foundation of rhythm, space, and groove, Hunter and Feingold engage in a fluid, improvisational exchange, pushing beyond conventional structures to create something raw, immediate, and deeply immersive. Their interplay unfolds like a dialogue – organic, unpredictable, and rich with nuance – where silence holds as much weight as sound. At its core, Different Strokes for Different Folks is an exploration of time and texture, where funk meets minimalism, and melody meets motion. Rooted in jazz, soul, and ambient influences, the project embraces both synchronicity and divergence, allowing each moment to breathe and evolve naturally. Villela began singing professionally as a teen and eventually moved to the Bay Area. A scholarship to New York's Manhattan School of Music and studies with the legendary Sheila Jordan cemented Villela's jazz credentials, and she returned to California as an artist on a mission to create fresh, original music born of her Brazilian upbringing and passion for jazz. She blends the ever-present samba of her native Brazil with jazz, blues, and songs from around the globe, inspiring the iconic San Francisco Chronicle critic Phil Elwood to enthuse, "Villela doesn't just sing – she actually dances with her voice on top of Brazilian beats." Villela will be joined on this concert date by Brazilian jazz-guitarist Romero Lubambo. Lubambo has an extensive and collaborative career. Vocalist Roopa Mahadevan, pianist and flautist Erika Oba, bassist Chris Trinidad, and drummer Kevin Amos integrate their multifaceted musical and cultural heritages to create a new diasporic sound that is uniquely Bay Area. Their multilingual repertoire features original music drawing on experimental jazz, Indian Carnatic traditions, Japanese folk music, Gregorian Chant, Original Pilipino Music (OPM) and more. ev_60745e16f19c.description: Tyreek McDole is a multi-award-winning Haitian-American vocalist from Central Florida whose soulful baritone and deeply reflective artistry are making waves across. Rooted in the belief that music is one of the highest forms of communication, McDole approaches performance as a space for healing, reflection, and collective dreaming – treating each concert as both offering and ritual. He first gained national recognition at the 2018 Essentially Ellington Competition at Jazz at Lincoln Center, where he received the Outstanding Vocalist Award, followed by winning first place at the prestigious Sarah Vaughan International Jazz Vocal Competition in 2023. McDole's critically acclaimed debut album, Open Up Your Senses, blends originals with freedom songs, spirituals, and works that speak to justice, unity, and ancestral memory. His sophomore album CHROMA is a continuation of his musical, intellectual and emotional story. Coleman is a master old-time fiddler, having recorded and toured internationally with celebrated artists such as trailblazing all-women stringband Uncle Earl, Rhiannon Giddens, Watchhouse's Andrew Marlin, and Aoife O'Donovan. ev_68f1d1671bae.description: FALL MAIN STAGE 2026 | Tickets on Sale NOV 2026 | NO LATE SEATING Written By Thornton Wilder| Directed by Guest Artist Jeffrey Lo A Stage Manager enters before us calling for time. But it's not a rehearsal they are calling us in for, it's real life. In Thornton Wilder's masterwork Our Town we experience life in three acts: "Daily Life," "Love and Marriage" and finally, "Death and Eternity." In a world where the possibility of humanity losing its grasp on reality looms large, the resonance of this classic reverberates today as strongly as it did when first written and in one of those most stunning scenes in the American cannon, we come face to face with what it is we have already lost. Hailed by Edward Albee as "the greatest American play ever written," this enduring story continues to ask us—generations later—how to use our time, how to love our time and how to run out of time.

ev_696b42b01075.description: Though John Carroll Kirby 's background is steeped in jazz, his signature sound blends genres and styles. A sought-after collaborator, he's worked with the likes of Miley Cyrus, Frank Ocean, Harry Styles, and Solange. Kirby earned a Song of the Year Grammy nomination in 2023 for his contribution to Steve Lacy's "Bad Habit." Since 2020, he's focused on his vibrant solo career—releasing 8 LPs and earning two Libera Award nominations for Jazz Album of the Year. His work has received praise from Pitchfork , The Fader , and the Los Angeles Times . As a film composer, Kirby scored the soundtrack for Cryptozoo , which received the NEXT Innovator Award at Sundance. He scored The Luckiest Man in America starring Paul Walter Hauser and Walton Goggins. Most recently, his music provided the soundtrack to the Oscar-nominated short film Retirement Plan. ev_69d78de9a386.description: Kim Shuck conducts the twice-monthly Virtual Poets series, with featured readers followed by an open mic on the 2nd Monday of each month and an all-open mic session on the 4th Monday of each month. Kim embraces the fool and jester qualities of being a modern poet and artist. She is a devotee of San Francisco, whose hills she wanders nearly always on foot. Her maternal grandparents met at the Polish Hall on Shotwell and she spent many hours with her mother and grandmother wandering the Mission St. Miracle Mile, taking books out of the Mission Branch library and watching aquarium fish on the ground floor of what used to be Hale's. She firmly believes in carrying a bubble wand, keys, pen and notebook and cats cradle string at all times. Kim, whose poetry draws on her multiethnic background which includes Polish and Cherokee heritage, and her experiences as a lifelong resident of San Francisco, served as San Francisco's seventh Poet Laureate, from 2017-2021. In 2019, she was awarded an inaugural National Laureate Fellowship from the Academy of American Poets, and a PEN Oakland Censorship Award. Members: Luke Henderson – violin Isaac Park – violin James Preucil – viola Ian Maloney – cello The ESQP provides a young ensemble opportunities similar to what the St. Lawrence String Quartet, ensemble in residence at Stanford University from 1998-2024, enjoyed in their early years through an intensive week of community outreach. In late 2002, veteran tenor sax player Chuck Peterson invited Scott to join Chuck's weekly "Jazz in the Bookshop" gig in a combo that featured three jazz veterans — saxophonist/arranger Bill Perkins, bassist Don Prell and drummer Jimmy Ryan. At the time, Scott was still in his early twenties and had only recently returned to the Bay Area, fresh out of Berklee College of Music in Boston. He's been on our stage virtually every month since 2002, and has led his own date here each month for the past dozen years. ev_6fce8652c613.description: Born in Oakland, California in 1950, Susan Muscarella began playing the piano when she was eight years old. Predisposed to improvising, she was encouraged by her first teacher to play the music she loved – jazz. Muscarella made the decision to become a professional musician while still in high school. In 1975, she was a composition major at UC Berkeley when UC Jazz Ensembles invited her to join its program's faculty. The extracurricular program's students inspired Muscarella to expand the curriculum into a bona fide program of study. She was promoted to Director in 1984, and, for the next five years, grew the program's enrollment, expanded its curriculum and produced the largest annual collegiate jazz festival in the country – the Pacific Coast Collegiate Jazz Festival. The Piano Trios of Bud Powell, Bill Evans & Keith Jarrett will explore the artistry and unique qualities of some of jazz's most beloved piano trios. Can't make it in-person? You can stream it! Click here to register.

ev_70980855fa78.description: FALL MAIN STAGE 2026 | Tickets on Sale NOV 2026 | NO LATE SEATING Written By Thornton Wilder| Directed by Guest Artist Jeffrey Lo A Stage Manager enters before us calling for time. But it's not a rehearsal they are calling us in for, it's real life. In Thornton Wilder's masterwork Our Town we experience life in three acts: "Daily Life," "Love and Marriage" and finally, "Death and Eternity." In a world where the possibility of humanity losing its grasp on reality looms large, the resonance of this classic reverberates today as strongly as it did when first written and in one of those most stunning scenes in the American cannon, we come face to face with what it is we have already lost. Hailed by Edward Albee as "the greatest American play ever written," this enduring story continues to ask us—generations later—how to use our time, how to love our time and how to run out of time.

Modúpue was named best jazz group of the year twice, in 2005 and again in 2010, by the Bay Area Blues Hall of Fame. Avotcja herself was named a "Jazz Hero" by the Jazz Journalists Association. ev_7cadbe1bc61e.description: In 1988, drummer Brian Blade moved to New Orleans to attend Loyola University. It was at this time that he met Jon Cowherd and the roots of the Fellowship Band began. Both Blade and Cowherd were able to study and play with most of the master musicians living in New Orleans, including: John Vidacovich, Ellis Marsalis, Steve Masakowski, Bill Huntington, Mike Pellera, John Mahoney, and Harold Battiste. In 1998, Blade and Cowherd began recording their own music with the group The Fellowship. Together with bandmembers Chris Thomas , Myron Walden , and Melvin Butler , they have performed at esteemed venues like the Village Vanguard and festivals such as the Ottawa Jazz Fest, Newport Jazz Fest, and the New Orleans Jazz Fest. Over their twenty-seven years as a band, they have released seven recordings. Their debut, Fellowship in 1998, Perceptual in 2000, Season of Changes in 2008, Landmarks in 2014, Body And Shadow in 2017, live from the archives in 2022, and Kings Highway in 2023. On this concert date, Brian Blade & The Fellowship Band will feature Blade on drums, Butler on soprano and tenor saxophones, Walden on alto saxophone and bass clarinet, Cowherd on piano, and Thomas on bass. Bria

ev_812e792ae273.description: DINNER SHOW with WRECKLESS STRANGERS Wreckless Strangers is a collective of friends and musicians carrying the torch for San Francisco's grand rock 'n' roll tradition. Their unique blend of "Ameri-Cali Soul" melds the contemporary blues stylings of Bonnie Raitt and Boz Scaggs; the songwriting sensibilities of Sons of Champlin and Fleetwood Mac; the swashbuckling Americana of the Lost Planet Airmen and Peter Rowan; and the funk of Sly Stone and Tower of Power with a dash of Grateful Dead and Jefferson Airplane for flavor and unpredictability. With soaring vocal harmonies and burning instrumental improvisation framed in concise and poignant original songwriting, Wreckless Strangers seek to honor and carry forth the brand of free-spirited musical fun and adventure that defines the Bay Area.

ev_86b8feff18ee.description: Chris Cain offers up a soulful stew of Memphis style electric blues. His powerfully deep vocals and jazz-inspired blues guitar riffs are unforgettable; uniquely his own, while reminiscent of the legendary BB King and Albert King. As a child, Cain attended concerts with his dad to hear many of the great blues artists of the time. When Cain burst onto the blues scene in 1987 with his award-winning debut album, he soon found himself sharing the stage and trading licks with a few of those legends, including Albert King and Albert Collins. Cain has released a dozen albums, each filled with soul-stirring songs pulled from his own blues drenched heart. His brand of blues is unforgettable. Now, with Good Intentions Gone Bad , Cain will find his largest audience yet, as his good musical intentions continue to pay off. According to Kid Andersen, there's no better blues player working today. "Chris Cain is the rarity whose blues prowess is so undeniable that he has gained everyone's approval. Ask any of your favorite guitar players who they think are the greatest living masters of the instrument, chances are they will all have Chris Cain at the very top of their list." Chris Cain Website Spon

ev_8708bef5fffe.description: Freddie Bryant 's latest recording project is his most intimate and his first complete album of solo guitar. Solo Bossa features 14 of his original compositions written over the last four decades. The title refers to bossa nova and many of the tracks have that classic feel made famous in the early 1960's. The music takes the journey from bossa to samba as well as baiao, bolero, waltz and a sultry ballad-bossa in 7/4. Solo Bossa was preceded by Upper West Side Love Story an epic song cycle featuring a nonet fronted by the acclaimed jazz singer, Carla Cook. It's a double CD/90min with sixteen songs with his "passionate lyrics and colorful music." (Carlo Wolff/Downbeat). It was featured in the NY Daily News and Downbeat listed it as "Best CDs of 2023." The all-star cast also includes Regina Carter on violin and saxophonists Donny McCaslin and Steve Wilson along with strings and a stellar rhythm section. Visit the website: https://upperwestsidelovestory.com/ for more info. Freddie received a master's degree in classical guitar from Yale School of Music and is in demand in the New York jazz and Brazilian scenes where he has worked with Eliane Elias, Tom Harrell and many others. I frame up the situation and then I push the button. I always want it to look exactly the way it looks to me." – Henry Diltz Henry Diltz 's work as an iconic photographer in the 1960s and 1970s is celebrated for his unique "fly on the wall" style portraits and his ability to capture intimate moments with some of the world's most influential musicians. Behind the Lens is a slideshow and storytelling experience – photographs that made music history and the stories by the man that took them. "I was a musician before I was a photographer," says Diltz. "So I started out photographing my friends who then all happened to become famous!" Diltz was the official photographer at the historic Woodstock festival in 1969, 1994, and 1999. He has shot over 250 album covers and continues to document the music scene in Southern California. ev_8f4d8bfa83cf.description: The well-oiled machine that is the road show of two intrepid archive divers, San Francisco's Tate Swindell and Vienna's Thomas Antonic, reaches Tate's home base with a program built around the recording of Allen Ginsberg 1980 Graz, Austria poetry event with Peter Orlofsky and musician Steven Taylor dubbed "America: Give A Shit," now a 2026 double lp release on Swindell's Unrequited Records label, and Antonic's recently published book, The Three Wives of Queer William S. Burroughs (Beatdom, 2026). (L-R) Taylor/Ginsberg/Orlofsky – photo by Saul Shapiro Tate and Thomas have lately been presenting programs focused on the Ginsberg lp in Budapest, Vienna, Prague and Graz. Thomas was last heard at Bird & Beckett in January 2022 presenting his previous book, Amongst Nazis: William S. Burroughs in Vienna 1936/37 . Tate is well known to San Francisco beats, baby beats and post beats for his production of cultural materials — books, lps, readings, concerts — derived from his archive explorations and personal contacts with the likes of Harold Norse, Gregory Corso, Neeli Cherkovski and countless others through the past couple of decades.

ev_922d62c3bff8.description: With a career spanning more than twenty years and six studio albums, Las Migas have become one of the most internationally acclaimed Spanish bands. They have performed in more than fifty countries and have been nominated four times for the Latin GRAMMY Award in the Best Flamenco Album category (2016, 2022, 2024, and 2025), winning the award twice. They have also received the prestigious MIN Award in 2019 and 2023 for their albums Rumberas and Libres , respectively. In the spring of 2025, Las Migas released Flamencas , a tribute to the essence and purity of flamenco. In this work, the band evolves its sound toward a more contemporary expression, wrapped in a powerful visual identity showcased in the video for "Celos," directed by renowned fashion photographer Javier Biosca. The recording won the Latin GRAMMY Award for Best Flamenco Album. Throughout their career, Las Migas have collaborated with a wide array of acclaimed artists such as Estrella Morente, Viva Suecia, Rozalén, El Kanka, Kevin Johansen, Tomatito, Josemi Carmona, and Loli Molina. These collaborations reflect the immense musicality and versatility of this unstoppable all-women band. Las Migas Website (Ticket Includes 5%

YOYOKA is a San Francisco Bay Area-based jazz fusion ensemble blending Japanese and American jazz fusion traditions with modern improvisation and vibrant rhythmic interplay. Led by bassist and composer Ken Okada , the group features GRAMMY award-winning saxophonist Ben Torres , DownBeat 'Rising Star' guitarist Hristo Vitchev , four-time GRAMMY award nominee Murray Low , and internationally acclaimed teenage drumming prodigy YOYOKA , known for her groove, musical depth, and commanding stage presence. The band has become a fixture of the Bay Area jazz scene, consistently selling out premier venues. Their international profile continues to grow, highlighted by a successful 2025 European tour, featuring sold-out performances at Barcelona's historic Jamboree and a headlining appearance at Bulgaria's Bansko International Jazz Festival. ev_9ab68ec866f5.description: Dima, vocals David Udolph, piano Chris Amberger, bass Akira Tana, drums Singing from the heart with a voice and style reminiscent of the early 50's, Dima was influenced at an early age by the music that surrounded her as a child: the classic sounds of jazz. She began to develop her style as a jazz singer while studying with Merrill Hoover, a well known jazz pianist best known for his eloquent accompaniment of vocalists such as Ernestine Anderson, Anita O'Day, and Mary Stallings. This rare opportunity set the foundation for her to establish her own unique approach to singing as she fell in love with the jazz standard. Known for her command of the lyric, beautiful soothing tone, soulful improvisation, and carefully chosen repertoire, Dima keeps alive the true art of the jazz singer. She's backed on this date by the best in the business, attesting to the respect she merits for her art.
ev_9ab68ec866f5.title: Dima + Four

ev_9af7c6a3fa72.description: The Garage Jam is an open, friendly bluegrass circle that meets the first and third Monday of every month, from 6 to 8 pm. All kinds of pickers show up, from rank beginners to grizzled veterans, plus folks who just come to listen and socialize. The repertoire is straight-up traditional bluegrass, although the occasional old-time or folk-inflected choice will pop up. The format is the old-fashioned song circle, with each participant getting a turn to call a song and set its key, pace, and feel. An experienced jam leader and bass player are always present to help keep things on track. Everyone is welcome — come on down!

ev_9b863080c835.description: Andy McKee is one of the world's finest acoustic guitarists; evident from the accolades he's received throughout his career. It's his youthful energy, attention to song structure, and melodic content that elevates him to a peerless level. McKee entertains both the eye and the ear as he magically transforms the steel string guitar into a full orchestra via his use of altered tunings, tapping, partial capos, percussive hits, and a signature two-handed fretting technique. McKee's crossover success has helped him to achieve millions upon millions of YouTube viewers, underscoring his emergence as one of today's most unique and influential artists. His song "Drifting" became one of the first YouTube viral videos, logging nearly 60 million views. He also curates his own annual guitar retreat called Musicarium . McKee's tour dates have taken him through Europe, Asia, Australia, and North America, including tours with legendary artists ranging from Dream Theater to Tommy Emmanuel. ev_9e66e163ba47.description: Doors at 6pm. Performances start at 6:30pm. Cantor Arts Center presents Forms & Frequencies, a Thursday night music series featuring musicians and sound artists from the Bay Area and beyond. Join us on Thursday, December 3 for a night of pounding electronics and unruly physicality with Xina Xurner and Tzotzona, with visuals by artist Christopher Richmond. Xina Xurner is a Los Angeles-based sadical and sexperimental music and performance duo with vocalist, sculptor, and performance artist Young Joon Kwak and musician and producer Marvin Astorga. Fusing industrial noise, power electronics, dark club-wrecking beats, electric guitar, and extreme vocal distortion, their body-shaking live shows unleash queer trans-femme rage, refusal, and joy. Creating an atmosphere that feels part club, part collective exorcism, Xina Xurner's performance will be paired with visuals by artist Christopher Richmond, whose alien and terrestrial landscapes juxtapose reality and illusion, using handmade props, special photography, and varied drawing styles to present multiple pictorial universes in constant kinetic interaction. ev_a41ad1380305.description: Born in Malaysia, raised in Western Australia, and now living in New York City, Linda May Han Oh began playing piano, bassoon, and electric bass before starting upright bass in 2002 at the W.A Academy of Performing Arts (WAAPA), where she graduated with first-class honors. Oh was a James Morrison Scholarship Finalist in 2003, an IAJE Sister in Jazz in 2004, and received the ASCAP Young Jazz Composer's award in 2008. She also received an honorary mention at the 2009 Thelonious Monk Bass Competition. After completing her Masters at the Manhattan School of Music in 2008, she now teaches the pre-college division there, and conducts jazz video conference master classes for high schools around the United States. Oh has performed with the likes of Joe Lovano, Steve Wilson, Vijay Iyer, Dave Douglas, Kenny Barron, Geri Allen, Fabian Almazan, Terri Lyne Carrington, and is currently the bassist for Pat Metheny. ev_a6a480508d3b.description: The Arun Ramamurthy Trio creates a groundbreaking fusion of South Indian Carnatic traditions with contemporary jazz, weaving masterful improvisations through ancient ragas and modern rhythms. Brooklyn violinist Arun Ramamurthy is a self-described Indo-jazz explorer who creates strikingly beautiful music fusing the spirit of raga music and jazz. Steeped in the Carnatic musical tradition of South India, but also versed in North Indian Hindustani forms, he's a prolific composer who has created scores for plays, dance productions, and other fellow musicians. His powerhouse trio features electric bassist Damon Banks , a global force also versed in West and North African rhythms, and drummer Sameer Gupta . This unique ensemble has performed on many prestigious stages, including Jazz at Lincoln Center, The Kennedy Center, Northampton Jazz Festival, Yerba Buena Gardens and Amsterdam's Bimhuis. The band's latest release, New Moon , shines a light on the teachings and wisdom of our ancestors, and the lessons we take on our own personal journeys. ev_ab66cd9adcf3.description: The Garage Jam is an open, friendly bluegrass circle that meets the first and third Monday of every month, from 6 to 8 pm. All kinds of pickers show up, from rank beginners to grizzled veterans, plus folks who just come to listen and socialize. The repertoire is straight-up traditional bluegrass, although the occasional old-time or folk-inflected choice will pop up. The format is the old-fashioned song circle, with each participant getting a turn to call a song and set its key, pace, and feel. An experienced jam leader and bass player are always present to help keep things on track. Everyone is welcome — come on down!

ev_adc61bfefe3a.description: Ricardo Peixoto's Brazilian Guitar will explore how various genres of Brazilian music can be expressed on the guitar. Uniquely Brazilian rhythms, harmonies, and chord voicings with open strings are utilized to create distinctive sounds in styles such samba, bossa nova, choro and baião. The class will analyze how the guitar closely translates and is integrated with the vocabulary of various Brazilian percussion instruments, allowing for a strong connection and interplay with the rhythm section, as well as in solo and vocal accompaniments. Have your guitar handy! Can't make it in-person? You can stream it! Click here to register.

Just passing through? Ten will do. BYOB and share your candy. Reservations ill advised, but call us if you want — 415-586-3733 The Potrero Hillbillies are Bird & Beckett regulars as a trio, as individual musicians (Joe Cunningham, Christopher Gray, Joshua Raoul Brody), as rabid book buyers, and as jazz aficionados. Their past efforts have included tributes to Harry Nilsson, the Kinks, the Band, the oeuvres of Merle "Please don't call me 'Merle "Ian Shoales" Kessler' Kessler" Kessler, Joe Cunningham, They Might Be Giants, songs with the name "Sue" in the title, and whatever the heck they feel like playing. It is that last category from which they will probably draw on Halloween. Ooh, scary!

ev_b9cabeeeb185.description: FALL MAIN STAGE 2026 | Tickets on Sale NOV 2026 | NO LATE SEATING Written By Thornton Wilder| Directed by Guest Artist Jeffrey Lo A Stage Manager enters before us calling for time. But it's not a rehearsal they are calling us in for, it's real life. In Thornton Wilder's masterwork Our Town we experience life in three acts: "Daily Life," "Love and Marriage" and finally, "Death and Eternity." In a world where the possibility of humanity losing its grasp on reality looms large, the resonance of this classic reverberates today as strongly as it did when first written and in one of those most stunning scenes in the American cannon, we come face to face with what it is we have already lost. Hailed by Edward Albee as "the greatest American play ever written," this enduring story continues to ask us—generations later—how to use our time, how to love our time and how to run out of time.
ev_b9cabeeeb185.title: MAIN STAGE | Our Town

ev_ba5298d190ec.description: Saxophonist Kristen Strom has been a mainstay on the Bay Area music scene for nearly two decades and is acclaimed for her beautifully rendered melodies, exceptional tonality, and accomplished musicianship. Strom has played alongside many well-known artists, including Manhattan Transfer, Gladys Knight, Natalie Cole, and more. In addition to her solo albums, Intention , Sojourn and Moving Day: The Music of John Shifflett, she has recorded on more than forty albums with various jazz and pop artists. Strom is on the faculty of The San Francisco Conservatory of Music, Santa Clara University, West Valley College and the Stanford Jazz Workshop. She is an endorsing artist and clinician for Selmer saxophones. San Jose Mercury News says of her most recent album, Sojourn , "It floats, swings, and touches on samba, and each track has a gem-like solo by the leader." A GRAMMY award-winning guitarist, vocalist, composer, and producer, Sharkey has become one of the most respected musicians of his generation – celebrated for his sophisticated harmonic sensibility, unmistakable tone, and ability to shape-shift effortlessly between musical worlds. Sharkey's guitar work on D'Angelo's landmark album Black Messiah earned him a GRAMMY Award and a position among the most innovative guitarists shaping contemporary Black music. As a solo artist, Sharkey has developed a distinctive, emotionally resonant sound that blends deep-pocket groove, virtuosic improvisation, and songwriter-driven storytelling. His latest album, RED , introduced audiences to his modern fusion of soul, R&B, jazz, and guitar-based narrative. His follow-up projects – each expanding his sonic palette – solidify his standing as an artist capable of speaking fluently to instrumental purists and mainstream audiences alike. ev_bde6224542f2.description: Throughout his career, trumpeter Ambrose Akinmusire has paradoxically situated himself in both the center and the periphery of jazz, and has also emerged in classical and hip hop circles. He's on a perpetual quest for new paradigms, masterfully weaving inspiration from other genres, arts, and life into compositions that are as poetic and graceful as they are bold and unflinching. His unorthodox approach to sound and composition make him a regular on critics polls and have earned him numerous grants and commissions. Born and raised in Oakland, California, Akinmusire (pronounced ah-kin-MOO-sir-ee) was a member of the Berkeley High School Jazz Ensemble when he caught the attention of saxophonist Steve Coleman. Akinmusire was asked to join Coleman's Five Elements, embarking on a European tour when he was just a nineteen-year-old student at the Manhattan School of Music. After returning to the West Coast to pursue a master's degree at the University of Southern California, Akinmusire went on to attend the Thelonious Monk Institute of Jazz in Los Angeles, where he studied with Herbie Hancock, Wayne Shorter and Terence Blanchard. ev_bf4f9126eb88.description: Jason Crosby and friends bring the music of Vince Guaraldi and The Grateful Dead to Kuumbwa. After decades on the road as one of rock's most in-demand sidemen touring with the likes of Susan Tedeschi, Robert Randolph and others, multi-instrumentalist Jason Crosby took time for himself. The result was his 2017 solo album, Cryptologic , and a relationship with Nashville's Blue Rose label. The album revealed the keyboard/violin/guitar player to be an honest, thoughtful lyricist and songwriter in his own right, singing and playing all the instruments on half of the tracks and bringing in Northern California stalwarts The Mother Hips for the rest of it. It was also inspired by the longtime New Yorker's earlier move to the Bay Area of California, where he found a kindred musical community that included The Mother Hips and the Grateful Dead's Phil Lesh and Bob Weir. ev_c0fbd41076a8.description: Joshua Redman acknowledges that the title of his new Blue Note album, Words Fall Short , could be viewed ironically. His previous and widely acclaimed Where Are We was his first to pair a vocalist with one of his many monumental quartets; yet Words Fall Short is anything but a comment on the saxophonist's last triumph. More accurately, his latest offering is an organic next step, a collection of previously unheard originals brought to life by inspiring new collaborators. "It's impossible for me to will a project into being," he says of the wide-ranging adventures he has embarked upon in what is now his fourth decade as a recording artist. ev_cad39d55754e.description: On May 11, 1987, pianist Michel Petrucciani , bassist Dave Holland , and drummer Eliot Zigmund took the Kuumbwa stage for a remarkable concert – a special stop on the trio's only tour – which featured these three giants of modern jazz in peak creative form. Petrucciani passed away in 1999, but his legacy shines in the new lovingly-restored release of this historic night. The never-before-released recording, titled Kuumbwa is available now from Elemental Music in deluxe edition as a 2-LP 180-gram vinyl set, with a sixteen-page booklet of liner notes and rare photos. We will celebrate the release of this Petrucciani masterstroke with 'Kuumbwa' – The Story Behind the Album , featuring a conversation between Kuumbwa Co-Founder Tim Jackson, and the album's producer Zev Feldman. You'll hear about the concert itself, the rediscovery and preparation of the tapes, the release production, as well as hear samples of the album. Can't make it in-person? You can stream it! Click here to register.

ev_cb04f7e8892e.description: In celebration of the centennial of trumpeter Miles Davis, the Marcus Shelby Nonet presents Birth of the Cool: Revisited , featuring music from the groundbreaking Davis recording performed in its original instrumentation. Birth of the Cool was not a singular session, but the composite work of a young innovative genius at the beginning of a long and storied career; surrounded and supported by a group of forward thinking musicians, composers, and arrangers. Birth of the Cool remains one of the most enduring recordings in the history of music – let alone jazz. The Marcus Shelby Nonet consists of nine San Francisco Bay Area master musicians, all of whom are a part of the Marcus Shelby New Orchestra: Heidi Tretheren on French horn, Remee Ashley on trombone, Mike Olmos on trumpet, Tony Peebles on alto saxophone, Melecio Magdaluyo on baritone saxophone, Jonathan Seiberlich on tuba, Greg Jacobs on piano, Shelby on bass, and Jemal Ramirez on drums. ev_ce4b1740fcf1.description: Leaving Dublin, Ireland where he was born and raised until the age of 22, David Nihill got drunk on travel and never quite hit sobriety of it. He has lived and worked in twelve countries and visited over seventy. His shows draw on his wide travels, cultural observations, attempts at language study, (occasional) international drinking session(s) and being a mildly confused immigrant. His latest show Taking Tangents promised to do just that :) David is the winner of the prestigious annual San Francisco Comedy Competition, (previous finalists include Robin Williams, Ellen DeGeneres and Dana Carvey) and runner-up in the Moth's largest US Grandslam storytelling competition. Also a bestselling writer, David recorded his debut special for Dry Bar Comedy in 2019, his follow ups Cultural Appreciation in 2023 and Shelf Help in 2025, and has been featured on TED.com, Sirius XM, Just For Laughs, Netflix if a Joke Fest, The Late Late Show, The Irish Independent, Inc, NPR, and the Huffington Post among others. A festival favorite, David's videos have also gone viral many times over with over 1 billion views and a social following of over 2 million people. David Nihill Website info/tickets/questi

ev_d152b889c474.description: Join us for the 16th Bita Prize for Persian Arts celebrating acclaimed Iranian musician Sima Bina. Sima Bina is a renowned Iranian folk singer, songwriter, and researcher. She is celebrated for her contributions to preserving and promoting Persian folk music and culture. Sima Bina was born in 1945, in Khorasan, Iran. Her passion for folk music emerged from her childhood experiences, as she grew up surrounded by traditional Persian melodies and rhythms. She began singing at an early age and was particularly drawn to the rich tapestry of regional folk songs from different parts of Iran. Her professional career grew in the 1960s when she started performing publicly and recording albums. Bina's distinctive voice and her ability to interpret traditional songs with authenticity quickly earned her recognition within Iran and abroad. Bina is also a dedicated researcher and educator. Throughout her career, Bina has tirelessly worked to collect, document, and preserve Persian folk music, traveling to remote regions of Iran to learn from local musicians and record their songs. ev_d17048e46f0c.description: The Wooten Brothers ' first public performance occurred in Hawaii in 1966 and established their identity as prodigies. Since then, Victor Wooten and the Wooten Brothers (brothers Regi, Roy , and Joseph ) have racked up ten GRAMMY wins, and twenty-six nominations. The youngest of the family, Victor, the brother who learned from all his older brothers, has been named one of the ten greatest bass players of all time by Rolling Stone Magazine . As a family band, they are second to none. The Brothers' music bends and defines genres; amplifies centuries, and spans continents. The Wooten Brothers began playing R&B before expanding to jazz, jazz fusion, classical, and country. They emerged in 1985 on Arista Records with their release, The Wootens , combining electronic music, funk, soul, disco, and boogie – offering only a sliver of the Wooten whole. The Wooten whole is all of that...and classical, and jazz, and country, and rock-and-roll. Connecting a musically deep past to a musical future, The Wooten Brothers build bridges across genres. Bar by bar, in live performances and on recordings, they provide an exhilarating 'connects-you-to-the-center-of-the-universe' sound. The Wooten Brother

Established in 2008 by Grammy-nominated pianist Murray Low, the ensemble has emerged as one of the premier academic performing groups of its kind. As prior recipients of a prestigious SiCA (Stanford Institute for Creativity and the Arts) grant, SALJE has been affored the opportunity to collaborate with several luminaries in the field of Afro-Latin music that have helped to elevate the ensemble's performance acumen, as well as aid in establishing Stanford as a vital West Coast center for Afro-Latin Jazz. Admission Information General – $32 | Seniors (65+) and Non-Stanford Students – $27 Price shown reflects total cost including $4 online/phone per-ticket fee.FREE admission for Stanford University students. ev_d653043fd3cb.description: Born in Norman, Oklahoma in 1985, Champian Fulton was recognized by The Detroit Free Press as the "most gifted pure Jazz singer of her generation." A pianist and vocalist with a career spanning more than twenty years, Fulton has released twenty albums as a bandleader and has performed in more than twenty-five countries. She has been recognized with numerous awards, including 'Album of the Year' in the NYC Jazz Record (2018, 2020, 2023) and 'Pianist' and 'Vocalist of the Year' by Hot House Magazine . She regularly appears in both the Jazz Journalist Awards and DownBeat's 'Rising Star' Critics Poll. An unforgettable performer, "Every song is a work of art in Champian's hands and voice" according to The Absolute Sound . Her "galvanizing presence" ( The New Yorker ) and her alluring musical presentation have made her, as The New York Times writes, "a charming young steward of the mainstream jazz tradition." ev_da02dd1e1410.description: Benny Green was born in New York City in 1963 and grew up in Berkeley, California. His father, who played the tenor saxophone, introduced him to jazz at an early age through his record collection that included Thelonious Monk, Charlie Parker, Billie Holiday, Ray Charles, and many founding voices of the genre. He began piano lessons at the age of seven, with his first paid performance at twelve. His major concert stage debut was in 1978 at the Monterey Jazz Festival as a member of the MJF High School All-Stars (now known as the Next Generation Jazz Orchestra). As a band leader, Green recorded two albums for the Dutch Criss Cross label in the late 1980s before signing to Blue Note Records in 1990. He remained with the label for ten years recording seven albums, as well as two albums for its Japanese subsidiary, Toshiba–EMI. Oscar Peterson named Green as his protegé in 1992, and chose Green as the recipient of the Glenn Gould Award for excellence in Music and Communication. He recorded many albums as a sideman throughout the 1980s and 90s, including a duet with Diana Krall on her GRAMMY Award winning album, All For You . He began studying with pianist Alla Epelbaum at The Calderone School of Music and Bob Mikula from an early age, and soon after enrolled in Jazz House Kids and NJPAC Jazz For Teens. Thompson later was admitted to The Juilliard School where he graduated with both his Bachelor's and Master's of Music degrees, and went on to further his education in Theology and the Arts at Fuller Theological Seminary. Thompson joined the John Pizzarelli Trio in 2019 and has performed with other major artists such as Christian McBride, Steve Turre, Catherine Russell, and Buster Williams. His recording debut was featured on Jazz at Lincoln Center's Handful of Keys album with the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra with Wynton Marsalis, and he has since released multiple recordings as a leader. ev_df0376b8d3c8.description: Brooklyn-based jazz chanteuse Laura Anglade is originally from the village of Brousse-le-Château in the south of France, though she grew up in the United States and spent several years living in Canada. Anglade's performances are a reflection of her roots: rich in simplicity, an appreciation for the past and finding wonder in ordinary moments. Anglade brings clarity and depth to interpretations shaped by the legendary voices of Sarah Vaughan, Ella Fitzgerald, Shirley Horn, Carmen McRae, Michel Legrand and Barbra Streisand, among others. Her 2022 release Venez Donc Chez Moi earned a Juno nomination, and in 2023 she was awarded the 'Prix Opus' for Jazz Concert of the Year. An international touring artist, Anglade has headlined jazz festivals across the United States, Canada, Mexico, United Kingdom, and Europe, captivating audiences through her innate storytelling. Her conversational style bridges the gap between singer and listener, making each performance intimate and personal. Her artistry has brought her to renowned stages including Paris L'Olympia, London's Royal Festival Hall, New York's Town Hall, and she is a regular at the Festival International de Jazz de Montréal. ev_df5ae652cba7.description: The Lenny Carlson Music Collective is a unique chamber ensemble that performs Carlson's original compositions along with standards. His musical directions converge in the genre of Americana, blending Jazz, pop, folk, and classical. A Los Angeles native and award-winning composer, Carlson has also been an accomplished jazz guitarist, producer, music professor and author. Since 2009, he has been resident composer for Jeff Sanford's Cartoon Jazz Orchestra. The Collective's premiere performance at Bird & Beckett on 1/22/27 will feature Kevin Gerzevitz, piano; Michelle Maruyama, violin; Carla Wilson, bassoon and Luke Kirley, tuba/euphonium. Kevin Gerzevitz's compositions and arrangements will also be performed. Carlson's recent discography includes the title and three additional selections on Jeff Sanford's Playland at the Beach CD (2023), available on Spotify and Bandcamp; Down by the Riverside: Theme and Variations CD (2022) on Bandcamp; and Nothing Wrong (2019), a Cartoon Jazz CD comprised entirely of his compositions, on Bandcamp. His passion for music was sparked at the age of three, when his grandfather gifted him a keyboard. Over the years, his artistry has reached audiences around the world. Whitaker's work as a performer and collaborator spans a wide range of stages and ensembles. He has appeared as a guest soloist with leading orchestras, including the Aspen Chamber Symphony and the National Arts Centre Orchestra in Ottawa. Whitaker won the 2026 GRAMMY for Best Arrangement, Instrumental Or A Cappella on "Super Mario Praise Break" with the 8-Bit Big Band; of which the album was also nominated for Best Large Jazz Ensemble. He is a three-time recipient of the ASCAP Foundation Herb Alpert Young Jazz Composers Award and has released four studio albums: Outta The Box, Now Hear This, Connections, and On Their Shoulders: An Organ Tribute . A graduate of The Juilliard School and a product of public education, Whitaker is deeply committed to the power of music to connect people and to ensuring that every child has access to music education. ev_e61ea4228006.description: The Klezmatics return with a powerful new album and live program. Celebrating forty years at the forefront of global roots music, the band brings We Were Made For These Times to the stage – a bold, cross-cultural project shaped by songs of protest, resilience, and radical joy. Blending Yiddish song with Black gospel, Latin rhythms, and avant-jazz, The Klezmatics transform tradition into a living, evolving musical language – urgent, joyful, and deeply relevant today. World-renowned and GRAMMY-winning superstars of the klezmer world, The Klezmatics erupted out of New York City's East Village in 1986 and revitalized klezmer for the new century with music that is steeped in Eastern European Jewish tradition and spirituality, while incorporating contemporary themes such as human rights and anti-fundamentalism with eclectic musical influences. They have released thirteen albums of wild, spiritual, provocative, reflective, and ecstatically danceable music, forever redefining and transcending traditional labels.
